text.p: Sappi Ltd said on Saturday that its net income for the six-month period ending March 31 was $0.04 per share, compared to $0.58 per share for the same period a year ago.
The company said that the second half of its 1997 fiscal year should be better, but that full-year earnings cannot be expected to match last year's.
Sappi, based in Johannesburg, South Africa, said in a news release that its lower results reflected poor trading conditions and low prices for pulp and paper products.
Excluding a $15 million charge for non-recurring restructuring costs, Sappi's earnings per share for the first half of 1997 would have been $0.077 per share, the company said.
Sappi said that in view of the results it has deferred a decision on a dividend until the end of the year.
The paper and pulp company also said it will sell non-core holdings to reduce its debt by about $220 million.
